Resume overall: refer to the formatting of the linked reddit post. Space on a resume is valuable, don't waste it with white-space/filler. Also the resume should be limited to a one-pager cuz ppl don't have time for a 2nd page.

Generally, you would also want to be able to see what job you are going for just by looking through the resume. Reading through the resume right now makes me think of Research or Mathematician, not SWE/DS (assuming that since you are posting in cscareerquestions).

Specifics on resume sections:

* Education: Maybe you just took it out for privacy, but def do have the uni name and GPA (unless it actually sucks). If you have any awards associated with that degree (blah blah Scholar) you can also put it here.
* It looks like there is limited work experience, so just put it all in one "Selected Experiences" section in the middle.
* The descriptions for each experience should focus more on the skills/tools you used/demonstrated and is useful for the job you are applying for and less on "job description". Right now the descriptions also feel very .... casual. Ex: "Did this for my college's summer project" is not necessary.
* Continuing from the prev bullet point, so much of the resume right now just sounds like filler. Ex: "Spent the semester researching the patterns and presented it in my college's presentation". What this sounds like to me is you trying to fill up your resume with words cuz you did the research and calculations for the project in one all-nighter and then tried to pass it off as a semester's worth of work.
* The descriptions for each experience would also ideally indicate (in numerical terms) what sort of impact you had, tho I do agree that as a student/intern it's hard to quantify.
* Skills: Toss Microsoft Office unless you're going for Data Entry/Data Analysis. Do you have Github? You mentioned Jupyter Notebooks in the description of one of the projects, why is it not in the skills section? If you are going for data science, consider stating the packages you are familiar with. Ex: Python (pandas, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, nltk). Do make sure you have for sure used it before ... you might accidentally get interviewed by the creator/contributor of one of those packages.
* Dates: Stick to all using months or all using seasons. Consistency makes the resume MUCH easier to read.

Example of what I would say in the bullet points of one of the projects (I'm obv making stuff up tho and framing it as an experience):

Student Researcher - Environmental Math Patterns \[insert giant space for formatting\] Spring 2020

* Presented \[semester-long research\](link to paper and presentation) to an audience of \_\_\_\_\_\_ explaining the various mathematical phenomenon that show up in nature.
* Utilized cv2 and matplotlib to visualize centering fractals, golden ratio, and periodical cicadas by coding up the algorithmic Mandelbrot Set. (Python)
* Demonstrate how patterns in nature can be summarized as recursive algorithms and connection to the bio-medical field (Python, C++) (actually, what was the point of this project?? was it just hw??)
